parts:
Hello dear all, I am new at the unmarked package. I am working with distance sampling and I am interested in appliying an HDS model with guanaco (Lama guanicoe) populations and I am having some trouble with the model script and with density estimation. I am working with two different sites each one has 500 kmsq. Below is my R-script. My questions are: 

 

1)     Which is the best way to choose among the key function? I looked at the histograms and ran null models for all the possibilities (hazard, halfnorm, uniform or exp); afther that I calculated the AIC foreach model and choose the model with the smallest AIC  . Is this correct? Is there any statics which help with this?

2)     I ran the models that you can see below but when I run sc5 and sc6  I have this alarm: "Hessian is singular. Try using fewer covariates or providing starting values." I tried to provide an starting value but another error appears: “Error in names(starts) <- c(lamParms, detParms) :   'names' attribute [5] must be the same length as the vector [2]. I can’t see any problem in my R-script. How can I solve this?

3)     I decided leave the two problematic models and to run all to others models just to learn when I do it and try to estimate density with the selected model which is the null one, it seems that all the transects from both sites have the same guanaco’s density. This seems wrong.

 

Perhaps my questions are too simpler to this group; in that case I would be grateful to receive  some advice of another group.  I’ve read Chandler,2015 R-script example and I am also reading the Kéry and Royle book “Hirarchical modeling in ecology”, but I am still having trouble with this,perhaps they are too advanced for me. Can you recommend something for starters?


R-script

distancia<-transectas_grupos[,2]

transecta<-transectas_grupos[,1]

 

yDat <- formatDistData(transectas_grupos, distCol="distancia",

                       transectNameCol="transecta", dist.breaks=c(0, 230,440,700))

parts:
Dear Antonela,

 1) I think it is ok to use AIC to choose among the key functions if you think this is an important aspect of your problem. Normally I recommend not choosing among detection models because they usually do not correspond to explicit hypotheses. I think the distance sampling community disagrees with me on this point, however.

 2) I do not see the problem with the starting values. Can you produce the exact R code and result?

 3) The null model has only a constant expected density per site and thus the fitted density is indeed constant. I suggest using the ranef() and bup() functions to produce estimates of site-specific abundance. This is discussed in some detail in various parts of the AHM book.  see p 234 and 439 and elsewhere.  I'm sure you can resolve your problem with starting values and produce better site-specific estimates though....

regards,
andy

Dear Antonela,

 1) I think it is ok to use AIC to choose among the key functions if you think this is an important aspect of your problem. Normally I recommend not choosing among detection models because they usually do not correspond to explicit hypotheses. I think the distance sampling community disagrees with me on this point, however.

 2) I do not see the problem with the starting values. Can you produce the exact R code and result?

 3) The null model has only a constant expected density per site and thus the fitted density is indeed constant. I suggest using the ranef() and bup() functions to produce estimates of site-specific abundance. This is discussed in some detail in various parts of the AHM book.  see p 234 and 439 and elsewhere.  I'm sure you can resolve your problem with starting values and produce better site-specific estimates though....

regards,
andy

El miércoles, 10 de agosto de 2016, 23:18:14 (UTC-3), Jeffrey Royle escribió:

Dear Antonela,

 1) I think it is ok to use AIC to choose among the key functions if you think this is an important aspect of your problem. Normally I recommend not choosing among detection models because they usually do not correspond to explicit hypotheses. I think the distance sampling community disagrees with me on this point, however.

 2) I do not see the problem with the starting values. Can you produce the exact R code and result?

 3) The null model has only a constant expected density per site and thus the fitted density is indeed constant. I suggest using the ranef() and bup() functions to produce estimates of site-specific abundance. This is discussed in some detail in various parts of the AHM book.  see p 234 and 439 and elsewhere.  I'm sure you can resolve your problem with starting values and produce better site-specific estimates though....

regards,
andy
